 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 13.01.2022 passed by M.A.C.T, Barwani in MACC No.412/2019 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Kailash vs Brajesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116061799/
1
The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the grievous injuries sustained by the appellant Kailash, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation amount of Rs.1,44,000/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
 Medical expenses -Rs.57,000/-
 Future medical expen -Rs.30,000/-
 Pain and suffering and  future loss of income -Rs.45,000/-
Special diet & transportation-Rs.8,000/-
 Attendant -Rs.4,000/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL Rs.1,44,000/-
 ============
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding adequate amount of compensation and the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

He further submits that the appellant had suffered fracture of left leg in the accident and he remained in hospital from 29.01.2019 to 02.02.2019, however, no compensation has been awarded for the grievous injury sustained by him, hence prays for just and and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the matter which does not call for any interference by this Court.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation for the grievous injuries sustained by him because of which he remained in hospital for 5 days.

The compensation awarded under the head of special diet, transportation and attendant are also on the lower side, hence in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
 Grievous injuries -Rs.35,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.30,000/-

Medical expenses -Rs.57,000/-
 Pain and suffering and  future loss of income -Rs.45,000/-

Attendant -Rs.6000/-
 Transportation -Rs.8000/-
 Special diet -Rs.8000/-
 ---------------

TOTAL Rs.1,89,000/-
Kailash vs Brajesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116061799/
2

Hence, the appellant is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,89,000/-
as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,44,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.45,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.45,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the rate of 6% p.m from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
